newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines to search for U-boat wreck off Patagonia.
newsitem.headline: Argentines to search for U-boat wreck off Patagonia.

text.p: Argentine coast guards and a professional diver were preparing to search this weekend for the wreck of a German submarine reported to have been sunk off Patagonia at the end of World War Two, the Navy said Friday.

Reports that emerged this week of sightings of a German U-boat wreck in the San Matias Gulf southwest of the southern city of Viedma have inspired speculation that it might have carried Nazi war criminals on the run from defeat in Europe.
Veteran local pilot Eduardo Chironi told reporters that some years back "flying over the area at low tide I saw the remains of a submarine."
Vidal Pereyra, a retired mechanic, said he saw it too.

"One day, I think it was March 1980, some friends said to me 'Let's go and see the submarine' and we went to the beach. There was a northerly wind with a very low tide and you could see it 200 meters (650 feet) off the beach, rusty and covered in barnacles."

Shortly after the war ended in 1945, the United States issued a warning that up to half a dozen U-boats were known to be somewhere in the Atlantic. Two U-boats surrendered off the Argentine beach resort of Mar del Plata in July and August.

There has long been speculation that Nazis carrying looted gold and artwork fled in U-boats to Argentina, a country which sheltered Nazi war criminals such as Hitler's confident Martin Bornmann, Auschwitz doctor Josef Mengele, Holocoast architect Adolf Eichmann and Erich Priebke, extradited to Italy for a war crimes trial there.
Divers from a local marine biology institute, led by Tony Brochado, plan to look for the sub with the help and guidance of a coast guard ship and plane.
